scope: i386 legacy AADD/AAND/AOR/AXOR CS/ES/SS offsets and implicit SS

unknown_native_target.contract: Representation-neutral shapes may omit the architecture. LLVM and HighC must require a valid x86APXAtomicPlan before dereferencing it or emitting native code.

ordinary_gs_hardware.operation: Set GS base so each specified signed/unsigned offset addresses one known volatile word; execute the generated segmented load and restore GS.

regression.before: HighC source case 1, AADD ES with MOV EAX,0x4000, passed &dword_4000 after native instruction decoding had already passed.
regression.after: HighC/X86 native-memory arguments share the raw addrStr owner; MedIR and HighC reuse one representation-neutral segment-offset predicate. Ordinary DS loads retain their relocated image objects.
regression.width_fix: Raw addrStr and intrinsic operands share the same view-selection rule, retaining source-width zero/sign extensions and arithmetic wrapping.

reference.fault_distinction: Protected-mode illegal SS addresses retain #SS; other segment address faults use #GP.

semantics.control: Optional byte 1 retains long-mode stack provenance; bytes 0x26/0x2e/0x36 retain an i386 segment offset. Mixed or mode-inconsistent controls refuse.
semantics.address: Original-width address arithmetic precedes native segment selection; offsets never acquire process-pointer relocation.
semantics.concrete: CS/ES/SS access refuses without descriptors before reading memory, storing bytes or publishing a result; the source remains unchanged.
semantics.instruction_effects: Original native RAO operation owns relaxed ordering, alignment/WB checks and arithmetic-flag preservation.

oracle.operation: Independent decoder locates native RAO boundaries. Unicorn executes surrounding i386 code while an explicit scalar completion updates memory at each boundary. Prefixes, offset wrapping, sources, return flags, cdecl stack and preserved GPRs are checked.

boundaries.host_source_transport: Recorders replace native operations only; host x64 Clang and NeverC runs validate operands and storage, not i386 instruction execution.
remaining: Concrete segment-descriptor environments and physical fault/atomicity qualification
Other instruction and state gaps in docs/x86-instruction-support.md

integration.external_results: All consumed source/IR/native-object exports are byte-identical to the qualified fixed-code corpus. C-compiled COFF objects differ only in their four-byte TimeDateStamp; command receipts differ only in temporary-directory names. Every other object byte is identical. The source-transport and controlled-i386 receipts remain applicable.

followup.defect: constAddress peeled integer views from typed constants, turning sext(i16 0xf234) into positive 0xf234 rather than 0xfffffffffffff234. The generated GS load failed on both SDKs.
followup.fix: Evaluate scalar constant widths, zero/sign extension, integer casts, bounded byte extraction and wrapped addition/subtraction in the shared address owner.
followup.stronger_mixed_roles: The same constant EAX value is used by an i386 segment instruction and an ordinary DS load in the atomic, compact and four-source pipeline fixtures.
followup.hardware_coverage: 20 ordinary GS loads compiled and executed at O0/O2 per SDK: signed/unsigned 16/32-bit parameters and constants, zero/sign extensions, wrapped sums, low-byte extraction and narrowing casts. PIE executables use a static volatile word and restore GS.
followup.external_results: All externally consumed C, IR and native-object exports are byte-identical to the already qualified fixed-code corpus. Only C-compiled COFF TimeDateStamp bytes and command temporary-directory names differ. Prior 1872 source executions and 36720 controlled i386 completions per SDK remain applicable.

publication_integration.scope_note: Qualification belongs to frozen 8bcd359a15. The published merge bd665c5a16 adds only reviewed upstream observed-window non-growth changes in SymMBA and its test/documentation; native x86 and C address code is identical.

cross_architecture.scope: AArch64 raw-SP provenance and typed pointer/source roles, including shared ABI return widths across AArch64, ARM, x64 and i386. No physical AArch64 execution is claimed.

publication_integration.external_results: All external C, IR and native-object inputs remain byte-identical to the fixed-code qualification corpus; only C-compiled COFF timestamps and command temporary paths were normalized. Prior source execution and controlled i386 receipts remain applicable.
